goal: Issue #688 -- the grip-fit rain exclusion ('any wet sample in the session') is too aggressive and drops ~55% of candidate weekends; loosen it to a graded / timed-running criterion that recovers usable dry coverage while still excluding genuinely wet running. PLANNING ENGAGEMENT ONLY: produce a mission frame and a frozen execute.json; implementation is a separate later engagement.

questions.question: Where does the 'rain exclusion' that dropped 20 of 36 weekends actually live -- production grip code, or the #678 spike?
questions.resolution: No production grip path drops a rain session. run_grip_batch walks every calendar GP x session_type and upserts whatever the fit returns; the only skip is the store.has() idempotency guard. rain_flag is consumed at exactly two places and both only multiply session_offset_sigma by RAIN_SIGMA_INFLATION=4.0. The 20-of-36 drop happened in the #678 spike's own (never-committed) candidate-weekend selection. The issue's premise is misattributed: the real defect is that NO production selection predicate exists, so every consumer invents one -- and the only universally-available signal to invent it from is the any-wet-sample bool.

questions.question: What wet signals exist in the canonical DB, and what is each one's real coverage?
questions.resolution: Four signals, wildly different coverage. sessions.rainfall (int64 blob = wet SAMPLE count) is the only universally-available one and is what rain_flag_from_raw reads. weather.rainfall per-sample rows exist 2022/2023 but are ABSENT for many 2024 sessions despite a nonzero sessions.rainfall count -- a fraction-of-samples rule reads 0/0 there. session_surface_features.session_rain_flag is populated 2022/2023 only, zero rows 2024/2025. session_surface_features.wet_lap_fraction is populated for session_type='R' ONLY -- every race 2022-2025, and ZERO non-race sessions in any season. lap_times.compound is universal and is the substrate wet_lap_fraction is derived from.
questions.code_evidence: .agent-work/issue-688/probe_coverage.py output (per-year, per-session_type counts of non-null wet_lap_fraction / session_rain_flag); .agent-work/issue-688/probe_rain.py output (2024 Australia/Q, Canada/Q, Canada/R, Spain/R, Austria/R, GreatBritain/Q, GreatBritain/R show 0 weather samples with nonzero rainfall counts); src/data/schema.sql:19,84,100-110; src/data/weather_features.py:224.

questions.question: Does this repo already have a precedented, map-sanctioned graded wet-exclusion seam?
questions.resolution: Yes. The fuel subsystem already solved this exact shape: a named WET_EXCLUDE_THRESHOLD = 0.05 plus a physics reader that consumes the STORED wet_lap_fraction rather than recomputing compounds, and the architecture map explicitly sanctions that physics->data read. #688 therefore does not need a new instrument; it needs the existing one extended to the sessions the grip fit runs over.
questions.code_evidence: src/physics/burn_rate_calibration.py:698 (WET_EXCLUDE_THRESHOLD = 0.05) and :709-745 (session_wet_fraction reads session_surface_features.wet_lap_fraction); docs/architecture/packets/physics.md:143-147, :161, :2833; src/data/weather_features.py:187-231; scripts/populate_wet_features.py; docs/architecture/packets/data.md:88-93.

questions.question: On real 2022-2024 data, does the issue's proposed 'fraction of wet SAMPLES' threshold actually discriminate a brief shower from genuinely wet running?
questions.resolution: No -- it fails in BOTH directions. False keep: 2023 Belgium Q has 1 wet sample of 95 (0.011) but 212 of 341 laps on wet tyres (0.622) -- a sample-fraction rule keeps a soaked qualifying session. False drop: 2022 Hungary R has 46 of 167 wet samples (0.275) and ZERO wet laps; same at 2022 Miami R, 2022 Great Britain R, 2023 Austria R, and 2024 Hungary Q (0.762 of samples wet, not one wet lap). Acceptance option A as literally written is the measurably wrong instrument; option B ('materially wet during the timed running') is right, and the lap-compound fraction is its operational form.
questions.code_evidence: .agent-work/issue-688/probe_rain.py output, 2022-2024 timed sessions (Q/R/SQ/S): per-session wet-sample fraction vs WET/INTERMEDIATE lap fraction, with the disagreeing rows listed above.

questions.question: Does the grip fit ingest wet laps at all -- what is actually at risk from a wet session?
questions.resolution: The fit never ingests a wet lap: the clean-lap reader hard-filters to SOFT/MEDIUM/HARD. So the exposure is not wet laps polluting the curve. It is (i) a mixed session's SURVIVING DRY laps sitting on a DRYING track, whose falling lap times are drying rather than rubber accumulation -- a direct violation of the monotone-rubber-in model the saturating curve encodes, and exactly what the issue's 'monotone-grip assumption still needs dry' caveat points at; and (ii) too few surviving dry stints, which MIN_STINTS_FOR_FIT plus the thin_fallback path already handles honestly. A severity threshold is therefore necessary but NOT sufficient -- a residual drying-track guard belongs in the plan.

questions.question: Which severity criterion do we adopt: weather-sample fraction, WET/INTERMEDIATE lap fraction, or a composite with an explicit unknown state?
questions.resolution: Adopt the stored WET/INTERMEDIATE LAP fraction as primary, expressed as a graded severity with an explicit UNKNOWN state (dry | mixed | wet | unknown) rather than a bare bool. The weather-sample count survives only as a fallback when the lap signal is missing; coverage-absent resolves to 'unknown' (widened, never silently 'dry').
questions.human_answer: Ruled by the Commander under the dispatching human's standing directive for this engagement: 'No human is reachable for this engagement, so wherever a step calls for a human decision, record what you would have asked, decide it yourself, and carry on rather than waiting.' The question as it would have gone to the owner: 'Your acceptance criteria names a fraction-of-wet-samples threshold first, but on real 2022-2024 data that instrument is wrong in both directions (2023 Belgium Q kept at 1 wet sample despite 62% wet laps; 2022 Hungary R dropped at 27.5% wet samples despite zero wet laps). Do you accept switching to the lap-compound fraction -- the instrument your own fuel subsystem already uses -- with an explicit unknown state?' Commander ruling: yes, adopt lap-fraction primary with an unknown state. Escalate on the owner's return if they intended the sample-fraction literally.

questions.question: Does the fix REPLACE the binary rain_flag, or add a graded field alongside it?
questions.resolution: Add alongside. rain_flag stays a non-Optional bool (it has live readers) and is redefined as severity != dry; the graded fields arrive as new nullable columns that the store's additive migration already knows how to ALTER-ADD.
questions.human_answer: Ruled by the Commander under the standing directive quoted in q6. The question as it would have gone to the owner: 'rain_flag is a non-Optional field on a frozen record with an additive-only migration contract. Keep it (redefined) or break it?' Commander ruling: keep it -- grip_store.py:130-131 states the migration never drops or renames, and removing the column would break every existing grip DB for no gain.

questions.question: Does the flat RAIN_SIGMA_INFLATION=4.0 become graded in severity, or stay flat with only the SELECTION criterion loosened?
questions.resolution: Grade it, preserving the conservative ceiling: 4.0 remains the value at full-wet and the factor interpolates down to 1.0 at fully-dry. This cannot make any session less conservative than today.
questions.human_answer: Ruled by the Commander under the standing directive quoted in q6. FLAGGED as the ruling most wanting the owner's word, because it changes stored sigmas that #664-class consumers read and it extends scope past the issue's literal text. The question as it would have gone to the owner: 'A flat 4x on a session with zero wet laps is the same over-aggression you filed this issue about, just in sigma form -- and recovering coverage is self-defeating if every recovered session arrives with a 4x penalty a precision-weighted pool then ignores. Grade the inflation too, or keep this issue strictly to selection?' Commander ruling: grade it with 4.0 preserved as the full-wet ceiling; the gate is planned so it can be dropped without disturbing the rest of the plan if the owner prefers the narrow reading.

questions.question: Does issue #688 own the data-layer coverage extension (populating wet_lap_fraction for non-race sessions), or is that a separate issue?
questions.resolution: This issue owns it. populate_wet_features_for_db must stop iterating races only and cover every session type, then repopulate the season DBs.
questions.human_answer: Ruled by the Commander under the standing directive quoted in q6. The question as it would have gone to the owner: 'The wet-fraction seam has ZERO non-race rows in every season, but the grip fit runs over every session type. Do I own the coverage extension here, or file it and ship a threshold with no signal behind it for Q/SQ/S/FP?' Commander ruling: own it -- shipping the threshold without the coverage would be a no-op dressed as a fix, and thin/missing Q is precisely the coverage the #678 spike named as the crux.

questions.question: Where does the usable-for-pooling SELECTION predicate live so consumers stop reinventing it per-spike?
questions.resolution: Ship a named production predicate in minimal form: one documented selection helper beside get_grip_at in grip_store.py plus a severity filter argument on GripStore.load. No policy framework, no config surface.
questions.human_answer: Ruled by the Commander under the standing directive quoted in q6. The question as it would have gone to the owner: 'The whole defect surfaced because selection lived in a throwaway consumer nobody reviewed. Do I ship a production predicate, or only the graded field?' Commander ruling: ship the predicate, bounded to one function plus one filter argument, so the next spike cannot reinvent the any-wet rule.

questions.question: What regeneration or re-batch does the change imply, and what does it cost?
questions.resolution: Two bounded regenerations, both planned as gates rather than assumed. Season DBs: the wet-feature populate is DB-only, idempotent and network-free, so extending it past races and re-running 2018-2026 is cheap. Grip store: the additive migration self-heals new columns to NULL, but graded values only populate on a re-fit, so run_grip_batch(force=True) is required -- a scipy curve_fit per session, the same cost as #663's original build.
